# Parosatajātaka (Ja 101)
**ID:** Ja 101
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Parosatajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja101
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Parosatajātaka* (Ja 101) is a short birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. Its single canonical verse states that even if more than a hundred foolish persons gathered together were to contemplate or think hard for a hundred years (*jhāyeyyun te vassasataṃ apaññā*), a single wise person who understands the meaning of what is spoken is superior [Fausböll 1877]. The commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*) explicitly observes that this story is entirely identical in background story (*vatthu*), exposition (*veyyākaraṇa*), and identification of characters (*samodhāna*) to the preceding *Parosahassajātaka* (Ja 99), with the sole variation being the substitution of the verbal form *jhāyeyyuṃ* [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral].
In the temple art and inscriptions of the Pagan period in Burma, this narrative was predominantly titled *Parosata*, though in the Lemyethna and Gubyaukgyi (Myinkaba) temples it was labelled as *Dutiya Parosahassa* [Win Than Tun 2002].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records curated cross-language parallels or significant machine-detected text reuse matches (score ≥ 10) in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
